messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Local Level Model Fitting
parts:
Function stan() in RStan does not use any parameter with dots; it uses 
"model_code" for the code, "chains" for number of chains, "iter" for number of iterations, etc.  Please check the doc.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Local Level Model Fitting
parts:
The biggest thing you can do at this point for speed is vectorize.  There have been lots of examples on this mailing list and there's also a discussion in the manual.  It may seem like more work to define a vector, populate it, then call the vectorized form of the distribution, but it's actually much faster due to the work it can save on calculating gradients.

Also, some of your transformed parameters should be defined in a "generated quantities" block following the model.  Basically, any transformed parameter that's not used in the model should be defined in the generated quantities block.  That way, they'll only be computed once.  This will only be a modest speedup, but I think it also makes the models easier to read.

Are you initializing the BUGS and Stan models the same way?  Those look like awfully tightly constrained deviation parameters and Stan takes very dispersed starting points by default.  (Try init=0 as an option, which will initialize the constrained variables to the middle of their range).

- Bob
